decisions.statement: The path handed on is the path the request arrived on without its query.
The method handed on is the method the request arrived with.
A POST is read into one buffer before the queue is reached.
A request that is no POST is handed on carrying no body.
The slot the caller handed in is handed on to the queue.
The request itself is handed on to the queue.
The queue is asked once for one request.
The response the queue answered with is the response handed back.
A body that will not read is answered 502.
A queue that throws is answered 502.
A 502 answer has the status text `Bad Gateway`.
A 502 answer has no body.
The error thrown is written about beside the line naming the fallthrough.
The fallthrough line names the method and the path.
The fallthrough line names the account as a hyphen.
Every line written here goes to a door the caller may replace.
A caller hands in the queue one request is run through.
A caller hands one slot to every attempt one request is served by.
Nothing here reads a page.
Nothing here chooses an account.
Nothing here forwards a request.
Nothing here retries a request.
Nothing here reads a clock.
A request whose url will not parse throws out of this handler unanswered.
A POST body reaching the queue is a whole buffer rather than a stream.
The pipeline the queue runs is wired by the caller rather than named here.
A 502 answered here names no reason a client could read.
The slot is handed on without the observer inside the slot being ended.

definition: one messages request taken in, handed to the queue and answered
